intent: Before I put a synthetic putting green in my Grand Strand golf-community yard, does my community allow it, where can it go, and how does the committee count it against lawn, green-space, impervious or grading rules?
distinctValue: Named Grand Strand golf communities give different written answers, and the difference runs between neighborhoods, not across the state line. Inside Barefoot Resort (North Myrtle Beach, Horry County), the master guidelines revised June 1, 2025 prohibit artificial turf, but the older Dye Estates guidelines (V5.4, effective 3/20/2023, recorded in Horry County 01/30/2024) exempt putting greens, require them to the rear of the residence and apply a 40 percent impervious limit; Leatherleaf's undated guidelines (file LLS_ARC_Guidelines_2024.pdf, uploaded 2024-07-10) never mention artificial turf. River Hills (Little River, Horry County) requires ARB approval for landscaping, 30 percent pervious landscaped space and a sodded front area. Sea Trail (Sunset Beach, NC) caps built-upon area under a State stormwater master plan and requires 40 percent sodden front-yard area in its 2019 standards (cover dated March 21, 2019; notice calls it the March 31, 2019 version). Brunswick Plantation (Calabash, NC) says 'No Artificial grass is permitted' in its minimum planting requirements, in the standards file named 'update 8.14.2026' on its documents page as of 2026-09-12. Ocean Ridge lists a committee but posted no standards on its public pages as of 2026-09-12. Each community also has a grading or drainage rule that a contoured green touches. The page promises only what the business may say about itself (free visit, measuring, checking the ground, a custom layout you approve, site prep and a base built for your soil); it does not claim the layout meets any committee's submission requirements, and tells readers to ask what drawings are needed. The national putting-green page, the Denver and northeast Florida putting-green pages and the Grand Strand town pages stop at 'bring your association requirements'; none quotes these rules.

Section III (printed page 8): "Artificial Turf & Vegetation: Artificial Turf & Vegetation are prohibited."
Landscaping (printed page 12): "Landscaping: This change requires an ARC application." ... "Artificial Turf & Vegetation: is prohibited."

Grading and Drainage: "Major changes in grading (For example: berms, mounds, retaining walls, etc.) shall be submitted for review." and "Water cannot be directed to flow onto a neighboring property."
Required exhibits: "In such case, the ARC's 30 day review period will not commence until all required submissions have been provided."
Search of the 20-page text layer: the words putting green do not appear.

Still the master guidelines linked from https://www.barefoothoa.com/dye-estates/ and https://www.barefoothoa.com/single-family-neighborhoods/ on 2026-09-12; the site's WordPress media library lists no newer master guidelines.

Order of versions: the master guidelines (revised June 1, 2025; PDF created Jun 5 2025) postdate Dye Estates V5.4 (effective 3/20/2023), and still list artificial turf as prohibited; the page says so and tells Dye Estates owners to get the green confirmed in writing.

Cover (PDF page 2): "Version #: V5.4 Final for Board/ARC Approval" "Date: 3/20/2023" "Effective Date: 3/20/2023"; page header "Deed BK: 4769 PG: 2082 Doctype: 082 01/30/2024 at 07:12:53 AM, 2 OF 97 ELECTRONICALLY RECORDED Marion D. Foxworth III, Horry County, SC Registrar of Deeds"

Landscaping (PDF page 37, printed 36): "With the exception of putting greens, no artificial grass, plants, or other artificial vegetation shall be placed or maintained on the exterior of any Lot unless approved by the ARC. See Putting Greens section for details. New home construction should show any putting greens on plans."

5.21.3 Minor Landscape Changes That Do Not Require ARC Approval (PDF page 38, printed 37): "This Section does not apply to new home construction." ... "The following, unless otherwise noted, does not require submission of an application nor ARC approval, however owners are still required to follow all ARC guidance, including, but not limited to, setbacks and view restrictions:" "Backyard and/or side yard minor landscaping changes of 500 sq. ft. or less:" with the sub-item "Installation of a putting green to the backyard (See Section Putting Greens.)"
5.6 Putting Greens (PDF page 41, printed 40): "All putting greens shall be placed to the rear of the residence. Impervious requirement does apply."

5.11 Impervious Surfaces (PDF page 28, printed 27): "No more than forty (40) percent of any lot surface shall be impervious to water absorption (excludes easements, wetland buffers, and road right of ways)."

https://www.barefoothoa.com/dye-estates/ links DES_ARC_Guidelines_V5_4.pdf (uploaded 2025-08-27 per the site's media library) alongside the master ARC_Guidelines_2025-06-01.pdf. The January 2026 'Dye-Estates.pdf' on the single-family neighborhoods page is a site map with no rules.
5.21.1 (PDF page 37, printed 36): "The landscape plan must be prepared by a landscape professional". The page does not claim our layout serves as that plan.

arb-manual page: "The purpose of the Board is to review and approve all new construction, additions, and/or alterations upon all home sites within the River Hills subdivision. This also includes all landscaping upon those same home sites."

sources.label: Sea Trail Master Association: Architectural Design Standards, Construction Standards, and Builder Information, revised and effective March 21, 2019 (publicly posted PDF; https://seatrailma.com/important-documents/ redirects to a login page)

II.H.8: "Lots within Coastal Area Management Act's (CAMA) Area of Environmental Concern (AEC) may have the permitted built-upon area reduced pursuant to CAMA jurisdiction within the AEC."

Landscaping, planting minimums iv: "Ground cover -- the front yard landscaped area requires a minimum of 40% sodden area. For remaining area, pine straw-mulch etc. is acceptable."

I.C: "The ASC shall meet on the third Thursday of each month"; I.G: "The Committee shall, within forty-five (45) days after receipt of each complete submission of the plans, advise the party submitting the same in writing"
Search of the text layer: artificial turf, synthetic and putting do not appear. PDF pages 40–43, 48 and 50 of 50 carry little or no extractable text and could not be searched.
Date mismatch inside the source: the cover says 'Revised and Effective March 21, 2019' while the notice and the file name say 'March 31, 2019 version'. The page gives both.

The built-upon list is 'not limited to' the named materials, so the absence of turf from it shows nothing about how turf or a green's base is counted; the page says the list doesn't settle it and tells readers to ask the committee in writing.

7.3 Minimum Planting Requirements, c.: "Lawn cultivar shall be indicated on the plant list. "ASC approval must be obtained for fill operations, shaping of land areas and drainage"
